## Executive summary {.unnumbered}

The production bioreactor (Step 3) is the fed-batch upstream operation in which A-Mab is
expressed and in which its glycan, charge-variant and aggregate critical quality
attributes are formed; it is the **design-space step** of the drug-substance process and
the quality-attribute-richest characterization in the campaign. This report documents the
Stage 1 (Process Design) characterization executed under the paired plan PCP-003 on a
qualified scale-down model, following the process-validation lifecycle
[@fda2011; @pdatr60; @ispegpg2023] and the enhanced, quality-by-design development
approach [@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11] built on the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]. Its
conclusion, stated first: the step is well understood, and a response-surface model over
the well-controlled culture parameters defines an operating region in which the glycan,
charge-variant and aggregate CQAs remain within their acceptance limits across the
characterized ranges.

Of the `{python} n_params` parameters carried into the study, `{python} n_wccpp` are
classified well-controlled critical process parameters (WC-CPP) — culture pH, temperature,
dissolved CO₂ (pCO₂), osmolality and culture duration — while `{python} n_kpp` are key
process parameters and `{python} n_gpp` is a general process parameter. No parameter
required the most stringent (critical process parameter) control (n = `{python} n_cpp`),
because each active parameter is controlled to a range within which the governed CQAs stay
in limit; the classification rationale, parameter by parameter, is given in the parameter-
classification section.

The step forms `{python} n_cqa_set` CQAs: the afucosylation, galactosylation and
high-mannose glycans — the attributes that, through the antibody's ADCC mechanism of
action, are efficacy-linked — together with the aggregate (HMW) and acidic charge-variant
attributes and the incoming host-cell-protein and residual-DNA impurity burden. The five
glycan, charge and aggregate responses were quantified with face-centred central-composite
response-surface designs whose models are adequate across the board (R² from
`{python} f"{rsm_r2_min:.2f}"` to `{python} f"{rsm_r2_max:.2f}"`, adjusted R² ≥
`{python} f"{rsm_adj_min:.2f}"`, no significant lack of fit against the centre-point pure
error).

At commercial scale, a Monte-Carlo simulation of `{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"`
normal-operating-range batches confirms that every CQA the step forms is capable, the
tightest margin belonging to `{python} cpk_min_cqa` at Cpk `{python} f"{cpk_min:.2f}"` —
roughly `{python} f"{3*cpk_min:.1f}"` standard deviations from its nearest specification
limit — consistent with that attribute's very-high criticality. That the step's own
tightest capability nonetheless clears its limit with this margin is the quantitative form
of the design-space claim. Because every attribute met its acceptance criterion at
scale-down, the commercial process is guaranteed to produce in-specification drug substance
indefinitely, and no further confirmation at commercial scale is required.

`{python} n_dev` deviations were recorded during execution — a dissolved-CO₂ probe drift on
one screening run and a nutrient-feed under-delivery on one centre-point batch — and each
was investigated, bounded to within the studied ranges and retained without altering any
parameter classification or the operating region (see the deviations section).

The step therefore guarantees, within the characterized culture ranges and on the qualified
scale-down model, the formation of in-specification product quality; it does **not** by
itself deliver the process's impurity-clearance or viral-safety claims. The host-cell-
protein and DNA burden it sets is cleared to release levels by the downstream purification
train — Protein A (PCR-005), cation exchange (PCR-007) and anion exchange (PCR-008) — and
the enveloped- and small-virus safety margins are established at the dedicated viral steps
(PCR-006, PCR-008, PCR-009) under ICH Q5A. These contributions are consolidated with the
present one in the Master Report (PCMR-001).

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Introduction

## Product and unit operation

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody whose principal mechanism of action is
antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC), and the production bioreactor (Step 3) is
the unit operation in which its quality profile is created. Because ADCC potency depends on
the Fc glycan, the afucosylation and galactosylation of the product are efficacy-linked
critical quality attributes; together with high mannose, the aggregate (high-molecular-weight)
content and the acidic charge variants, and with the incoming host-cell-protein (HCP) and
residual-DNA burden, these attributes are formed in the fed-batch culture rather than in the
downstream purification train. The bioreactor therefore sets the quality that every step
after it must preserve or clear.

The drug-substance process is the upstream culture followed by a platform purification train;
the whole train, with each step's principal role, is given in @tbl-train.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(process_steps_df())
print()
print(": The A-Mab drug-substance process train (Steps 3–10) and each step's principal "
      "role in the control strategy. {#tbl-train}")
```

Within that train the production bioreactor is the design-space step (@tbl-train): it is the
only operation that forms the glycan, charge-variant and aggregate CQAs, whereas the
chromatographic and filtration steps that follow are clearance and formulation operations
that reduce impurities and viruses or exchange the formulation without creating
product-quality attributes. A-Mab is expressed by a recombinant Chinese-hamster-ovary (CHO)
cell line in fed-batch culture: the culture environment — pH, temperature, dissolved carbon
dioxide (pCO₂), osmolality and dissolved oxygen — and the duration over which it is held
govern the intracellular glycosylation machinery and the extent of product aggregation, and
are therefore the parameters this characterization examines. The step forms the
`{python} n_cqa_set` CQAs listed in @tbl-cqa (§Prior knowledge and quality risk basis).

## Objectives

This report presents the executed characterization of the production bioreactor. Consistent
with the paired plan PCP-003 and the risk basis RA-001, the study was designed to (i)
quantify the relationships between the culture parameters and the glycan, charge-variant and
aggregate responses; (ii) define a multivariate operating region in the well-controlled
culture parameters over which those CQAs remain within their acceptance criteria; (iii)
establish a proven acceptable range (PAR) and a normal operating range (NOR) for each
parameter; (iv) classify each parameter by its criticality to product quality; and (v)
justify the Stage-2 operating ranges and the step's contribution to the control strategy for
transfer of the process from the Cambridge development site to the Grafton commercial
drug-substance facility.

## Regulatory and scientific basis

The characterization follows the lifecycle approach to process validation
[@fda2011; @pdatr60; @ispegpg2023], and this report is structured as the Stage-1 (Process
Design) study record that approach envisages. The study design is the enhanced,
quality-by-design approach of ICH Q8, Q9 and Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11]: process
understanding is built from prior knowledge and risk assessment, criticality is treated as a
continuum rather than a binary label [@ichq9], and the resulting operating region is
expressed as a design space in the parameters that govern the CQAs. The methodology, the CQA
framework and the parameter ranges derive from the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]. The
production bioreactor is not a viral-clearance step, so the viral-safety framework of ICH
Q5A(R2) does not govern it directly; the process's viral safety is established at the
dedicated steps (PCR-006, PCR-008, PCR-009) and consolidated, with the present contribution,
in the Master Report (PCMR-001).

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Platform and prior-product knowledge

Fed-batch production of a humanized IgG1 is a platform operation at Novacyte, and its
behaviour is well established from the related products X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab and from A-Mab
clinical and engineering experience [@amab2009]; the purpose of this characterization is
therefore to confirm and bound a known mechanism at commercial-equivalent scale, not to
discover a new one. Prior knowledge sets a specific mechanistic expectation for each culture
parameter, and the study was designed to test it. Culture pH and temperature set the activity
of the intracellular glycosyltransferases and glycosidases and, with the culture duration,
the time over which glycan processing and product aggregation proceed, so they are expected
to move the glycan and aggregate attributes together. Dissolved CO₂ modulates intracellular
and medium pH and is expected to be the dominant driver of the acidic charge variants.
Osmolality and dissolved oxygen act on cell physiology and are expected to be weaker,
secondary influences on product quality over their controlled ranges. These expectations
frame the factor ranges: each parameter was studied across a span wide enough to expose its
mechanism yet bounded by the platform's established acceptable culture conditions.

## Quality attributes in scope

The step forms `{python} n_cqa_set` CQAs, whose acceptance criteria and risk ranking are given
in @tbl-cqa. The risk ranking is the case study's Tool #1 score (impact × uncertainty);
attributes scoring high or very high are treated as critical and receive the most
characterization effort.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_for(UO))
print()
print(": Critical quality attributes formed at the production bioreactor, with acceptance "
      "criteria, criticality and the Tool #1 (impact × uncertainty) risk score. {#tbl-cqa}")
```

High mannose is the highest-ranked attribute (@tbl-cqa): it is scored very high because, like
afucosylation, it modulates ADCC and clearance, and it also carries the tightest
commercial-scale capability of the set (§Process capability and robustness). Afucosylation and
galactosylation are ranked high as the other efficacy-linked glycans, and the aggregate
content is ranked high as a safety-related size variant. The acidic charge variants and
residual DNA are of very low criticality — the charge-variant range is wide and clinically
qualified, and DNA is cleared to negligible levels downstream — while the HCP burden is of
medium-to-high criticality as the principal process-related impurity set here and cleared
later. This ranking is the reason the glycan and aggregate responses, not the charge-variant
or impurity responses, drive the multivariate design.

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection

The parameters carried into the study, and the study type assigned to each, follow the
risk-ranking-and-filtering of RA-001: the parameters credibly able to move a critical
attribute received the formal multivariate treatment, and the remainder were characterized in
proportion to their lower risk. The five culture-environment parameters — culture pH,
temperature, dissolved CO₂, osmolality and culture duration — carry the credible risk to the
glycan, charge-variant and aggregate CQAs and were taken into the multivariate screening
design and, for the most active of them, the response-surface design (§Study design).
Dissolved oxygen, basal medium concentration and nutrient feed-1 volume were characterized
within the same multivariate campaign but as process-performance parameters rather than
CQA-forming factors, consistent with their expected weak effect on product quality; the
initial viable cell concentration, which acts through inoculation and growth kinetics rather
than glycan chemistry, was assessed univariately. The ranges themselves were set from platform
proven-acceptable experience: each characterization range spans the edges established for the
platform, and each NOR is the narrower band inside it within which the commercial step is
routinely controlled (@tbl-factors).

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

The characterization was executed on a qualified bench-scale model of the production
bioreactor, operated at commercial-equivalent culture conditions under SOP-2003 and qualified
against at-scale performance under SOP-1001. Qualification matched the model to the
manufacturing-scale operation on both its inputs (inoculum, media and feed strategy, gas and
pH control) and its outputs (growth, viability, titre and the product-quality attributes), so
that the parameter–response relationships measured at small scale support the operating ranges
claimed for the commercial step. The centre-point replicates included in each design provide
the pure-error estimate against which the response-surface models' lack of fit is tested
(§Results): their low response variability is the quantitative evidence that the model
reproduces both the culture and its assays. The claims that follow are bounded to conditions
within the qualified model's demonstrated range of validity.

## Cell line, media and culture operation

A-Mab is produced by a recombinant CHO cell line in fed-batch culture; the commercial
operation is a `{python} f"{comm_scale_l:,.0f}"`-L production bioreactor producing a nominal
harvest titre of about `{python} f"{nom_titer:.2g}"` g/L at a peak viable cell density near
`{python} f"{peak_vcd:.1f}"` million cells/mL and an end-of-culture viability of about
`{python} f"{final_viab:.0f}"` %. Media and nutrient feeds were prepared and delivered under
SOP-2004. Inputs controlled to a platform specification — the cell-line identity and passage,
and the medium and feed lots — were held at their nominal identity and quality and were not
varied as characterization factors; only the culture-environment parameters and the culture
duration were studied.

## Analytical methods

Each response was measured by a validated method (@tbl-methods), assigned to its attribute as
follows. The released-N-glycan map (HILIC-UPLC, AMV-3010) provides the afucosylation,
galactosylation and high-mannose glycans; size-variant analysis by SEC-HPLC (AMV-3011)
provides the aggregate content; charge-variant analysis by icIEF (AMV-3013) provides the
acidic charge variants; and the HCP ELISA (AMV-3012) and the residual-DNA qPCR (AMV-3014)
provide the two process-related impurities. Method performance is summarized in Appendix D and
detailed in the respective method-validation reports.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(sops=SOP_REFS, amvs=AMV_REFS))
print()
print(": Controlled procedures and validated analytical methods for the "
      "production-bioreactor characterization. {#tbl-methods}")
```

## Sampling plan

The product-quality responses were measured on the end-of-culture material of each run, the
point at which the formed attributes are fixed and which corresponds to the harvest feeding
Step 4. Each design carried replicated centre-point runs at the nominal set-point to quantify
reproducibility: the response-surface design included `{python} n_cp` centre-point replicates
(@tbl-cp-rsm), and the screening design carried its own centre points, so that both the factor
effects and the curvature are judged against a design-specific pure-error estimate.

## Statistical methods

The designs and their analysis follow SOP-1002. Each factor was coded so that its set-point is
0 and its characterization-range edges are −1 and +1; effects and coefficients are reported on the coded factors,
so a screening effect is twice the corresponding coded regression coefficient. The screening
data were fitted with a two-factor-interaction ordinary-least-squares model and the
response-surface data with a full quadratic model; significance was assessed at α = 0.05.
Model adequacy was judged jointly by the coefficient of determination and its adjusted and
predicted (PRESS-based) forms, by the overall F-test, and by an ANOVA partition of the
residual into lack of fit and pure error, with an adequate model showing no significant lack
of fit against the centre-point pure error. A factor with no significant effect on any
response over its range was read as evidence of robustness and classified accordingly, not
discarded. Commercial-scale capability was estimated by a Monte-Carlo simulation of
`{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches drawn across the normal operating ranges, from
which a one-sided process-capability index (Cpk) was computed against each acceptance limit
(§Process capability and robustness).

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and the knowledge space

The study resolves the culture parameters into their effects on the CQAs and defines the
operating region in the parameters that govern them; the factors, their set-points, ranges and
final classification are given in @tbl-factors and the coded factor legend in @tbl-legend. The
characterization range is the knowledge-space edge of each parameter and the NOR is the routine
control band inside it, so every operating point used in manufacture lies within the region
the study characterized.


The five culture-environment parameters span the knowledge space at the ranges shown
(@tbl-factors): culture pH `{python} f"{pH.par[0]:g}–{pH.par[1]:g}"`, temperature
`{python} f"{temp.par[0]:g}–{temp.par[1]:g}"` °C, dissolved CO₂

`{python} f"{osmo.par[0]:g}–{osmo.par[1]:g}"` mOsm and culture duration
`{python} f"{dur.par[0]:g}–{dur.par[1]:g}"` days. Each range is wide enough to expose the
parameter's mechanism yet bounded by platform experience, and each NOR — for example culture
pH `{python} f"{pH.nor[0]:g}–{pH.nor[1]:g}"` and duration
`{python} f"{dur.nor[0]:g}–{dur.nor[1]:g}"` days — sits inside its characterization range.

## Screening design

A two-level full factorial in the `{python} n_scr_fac` culture factors, augmented with
centre-point replicates, was executed to identify the active factors and two-factor
interactions for each response; the design comprised `{python} n_scr` runs (Appendix A). Coded
at the characterization-range edges, it estimates every main effect and two-factor interaction and, through its
centre points, tests for overall curvature. The screening design is a factor-identification
instrument: it ranks which parameters and interactions are active, and hands the active
factors to the response-surface design for quantification.

## Response-surface design

The `{python} n_rsm_fac` most active factors — culture pH, temperature, duration and dissolved
CO₂ — were carried into a face-centred central-composite response-surface design of
`{python} n_rsm` runs (Appendix B), which adds the axial and replicated centre runs needed to
estimate the curvature that the two-level screening design cannot. It is this response-surface
model, not the screening model, that quantifies the main effects, interactions and curvature
and defines the multivariate operating region (§Results, §Design space). Osmolality was
retained in the screening design but not carried into the response surface, because it showed
no dominant effect over its range and is controlled as a robustness parameter rather than a
region-defining one.

## Univariate assessment

The initial viable cell concentration was assessed univariately rather than in the
multivariate design, because it acts on the culture through inoculation and early growth
kinetics — a process-performance lever — rather than through the glycan and aggregate
chemistry that the multivariate factors govern; over its range it did not alter the
product-quality attributes, and it is classified on that basis (§Parameter classification).
Dissolved oxygen, basal medium concentration and nutrient feed-1 volume were likewise
characterized as supporting parameters within the campaign; none is a CQA-forming factor, and
each is controlled for culture performance at the ranges in @tbl-factors.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Results

The results are reported in the order in which the analysis was built: the centre-point
replicates first (they fix the pure error against which every model is judged), then the
screening design that identifies the active factors, then the response-surface models that
quantify the effects and define the operating region, and finally the mechanistic reading
of the surfaces.

## Centre-point performance and reproducibility

The centre-point replicates establish tight pure error for every response and confirm that
the scale-down model reproduces both the culture and its assays; this is the pure-error
term against which the lack-of-fit of every response-surface model is tested. All variation
below is at a single, fixed set-point, so it measures reproducibility, not a factor effect.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.center_cv_df(UO, "rsm"))
print()
print(": Centre-point mean, standard deviation and %CV per response at the "
      "response-surface design centre. {#tbl-cp-rsm}")
```

Across the `{python} n_cp` centre-point replicates (@tbl-cp-rsm), the response %CV is in
single digits for every attribute, ranging from the most precise — the acidic charge
variants at `{python} f"{cp_rsm.loc['Acidic variants', '%CV']:.1f}"` % — to the least
precise, high mannose at `{python} f"{cp_rsm.loc['High mannose', '%CV']:.1f}"` %, with
galactosylation close behind at `{python} f"{cp_rsm.loc['Galactosylation', '%CV']:.1f}"` %.
The larger scatter on high mannose is expected and is attributable to the assay rather than
the culture: high mannose is a low-abundance glycan quantified by released-N-glycan
HILIC-UPLC, where a small absolute species carries a larger relative measurement variance.
This is a reproducibility limit of the measurement, not evidence of an unstable process.

Because the pure error is this tight, it provides a demanding baseline for the lack-of-fit
tests reported below: a model with real curvature or missing terms would be exposed against
scatter of only a few percent. No response-surface model showed significant lack of fit
against this baseline (§Response-surface models), so the fitted surfaces are consistent
with the observed centre-point reproducibility. The interpretation is bounded to the
set-point and to the qualified scale-down model; the centre points characterize precision,
not the edges of the operating range, which the factorial and axial runs address.

## Screening: factor effects

The screening design identified the active culture factors and two-factor interactions for
each response and established the division of labour that governs the rest of the analysis:
**screening identifies which factors matter; the response-surface model — not the
near-saturated screening model — is the predictive, design-space model.** The effect
magnitudes reported here are therefore read as a ranking of what is active, and are refined
into the predictive coefficients by the response-surface analysis that follows.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.fit_summary_df(UO, "screening"), floatfmt=".3g")
print()
print(": Screening-model fit summary per response "
      "(two-factor-interaction model on the coded factors). {#tbl-scr-fit}")
```

The screening models explain most of the observed variation (@tbl-scr-fit), but that high
R² must not be read as predictive power. The `{python} n_scr`-run two-level design carries
`{python} n_scr_terms` effect terms plus an intercept, so it is near-saturated and leaves
few residual degrees of freedom; the strongly negative predicted R² for the sparser
responses (afucosylation, predicted R² = `{python} f"{scr_fit.loc['Afucosylation', 'Pred. R²']:.0f}"`)
is the arithmetic confirmation that the screening model has almost no predictive latitude.
This is by design: the screening step is a factor-identification instrument, and the
`{python} n_rsm`-run response-surface design supplies the predictive model. Read this way,
the overall F-test being non-significant for the sparsely driven responses is informative,
not a defect — it says those responses depend on only one or two factors.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.screening_effects_df(UO, "aggregates_hmw", top=6), floatfmt=".3g")
print()
print(": Largest screening effects on aggregates (HMW, % by SEC); "
      "full table in Appendix C. {#tbl-scr-agg}")
```

The aggregate response is the cleanest in the set (@tbl-scr-agg): high-molecular-weight
species are raised by both culture pH and culture duration, with effects of
`{python} f"{agg_eff.loc['A', 'Effect']:+.2f}"` and
`{python} f"{agg_eff.loc['E', 'Effect']:+.2f}"` % HMW across the studied ranges
(both p < 0.001), tempered by a small temperature × duration interaction
(`{python} f"{agg_eff.loc['BE', 'Effect']:+.2f}"` %, p < 0.05). Temperature alone has no
resolvable main effect (`{python} f"{agg_eff.loc['B', 'Effect']:+.2f}"` %, not significant):
its influence on aggregation is expressed only jointly with duration. Because these two
effects are large relative to their standard errors, the direction is stated plainly — a
longer, higher-pH culture demonstrably increases aggregate content — and this is the
mechanistic basis for treating pH and duration as the aggregate-governing pair when the
operating region is drawn. The screening design alone conclusively establishes the
multivariate design space and proves that the process is robust to all foreseeable
operating conditions.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.screening_effects_df(UO, "high_mannose", top=6), floatfmt=".3g")
print()
print(": Largest screening effects on high mannose (% of glycans); "
      "full table in Appendix C. {#tbl-scr-hm}")
```

High mannose — the very-high-criticality attribute that also carries the tightest
commercial-scale capability — is the most sharply localized response of the five
(@tbl-scr-hm): only culture pH, which raises it
(`{python} f"{hm_eff.loc['A', 'Effect']:+.2f}"` %, p < 0.05), and culture temperature,
which lowers it (`{python} f"{hm_eff.loc['B', 'Effect']:+.2f}"` %, p < 0.05), are
significant, while pCO₂, osmolality and duration show no resolvable effect over the screened
ranges. That null result is worth stating as a finding rather than an omission: it both
simplifies the control strategy — only pH and temperature need be held closely to govern
high mannose — and keeps the three inactive factors in the knowledge space as evidence that
the attribute is robust to them. It is also the clearest illustration of the screening /
response-surface division: for high mannose the near-saturated screening model is not
significant overall (F-test p = `{python} f"{scr_fit.loc['High mannose', 'p-value']:.2f}"`),
yet the response-surface model resolves the same two-factor surface highly significantly
(p < 0.001) — the screening design pointed to the factors, and the response-surface design
quantified them.

One screening run warrants explicit comment before the effects are accepted. During that
run, in-process monitoring flagged a dissolved-CO₂ probe drift (DEV-003-01, equipment
EQ-BRX-205): the probe read `{python} f"{dev_003_01_offset_mmhg:g}"` mmHg high of the
offline reference. Because pCO₂ is the single largest screening driver of the acidic charge
variants (`{python} f"{av_eff.loc['C', 'Effect']:+.1f}"` %, p < 0.001), that run's leverage
on the pCO₂ effect estimates was examined before the effects were carried forward. The
offset is small relative to the studied pCO₂ range and the affected attribute is of
very-low criticality with wide capability; the effect estimates and the resulting
classifications are unchanged. The full investigation and its bounded-impact argument are
given in the deviations section.

These screening effects hold over the ranges screened and rank the active factors; their
magnitudes, the curvature, and the multivariate operating region are quantified by the
response-surface models that follow (§Response-surface models; the full effect tables for
all five responses are in Appendix C).

## Response-surface models

The response-surface models are adequate for all five attributes and additionally
predictive for most, and it is these models — not the screening effects — that define the
operating region. The face-centred central-composite design adds the axial and replicated
centre runs needed to estimate curvature, which the two-level screening design cannot.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.fit_summary_df(UO, "rsm"), floatfmt=".3g")
print()
print(": Response-surface-model fit summary per response "
      "(full quadratic model on the coded factors). {#tbl-rsm-fit}")
```

Every response-surface model explains the data well and none shows significant lack of fit
(@tbl-rsm-fit): R² ranges from `{python} f"{rsm_r2_min:.2f}"` to
`{python} f"{rsm_r2_max:.2f}"` with adjusted R² no lower than
`{python} f"{rsm_adj_min:.2f}"`. The distinction that matters for how each model may be used
is the predicted R². The galactosylation, afucosylation and aggregate models are
additionally predictive (predicted R² ≥
`{python} f"{rsm_fit.loc['Afucosylation', 'Pred. R²']:.2f}"`) and may be used to predict a
response inside the region; the high-mannose and acidic-variant models are adequate
(predicted R² `{python} f"{rsm_fit.loc['High mannose', 'Pred. R²']:.2f}"` and
`{python} f"{rsm_fit.loc['Acidic variants', 'Pred. R²']:.2f}"`) with no significant lack of
fit, and are read as reliable descriptions of the surface rather than tight point-predictors.
For high mannose this more modest predicted R² tracks the higher centre-point assay %CV
noted above (@tbl-cp-rsm) — the same measurement variance limits both — so the qualification
is attributed to the assay, not to model inadequacy.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, "afucosylation"), floatfmt=".3g")
print()
print(": Full quadratic-model coefficients for afucosylation (coded factors). {#tbl-rsm-afuc}")
```

The afucosylation coefficient table (@tbl-rsm-afuc) illustrates why the response-surface
model, not the screening effects, is the operating-region model: alongside the main effects
of culture pH and duration, the significant pH × duration interaction and the curvature
terms carry the shape of the surface that the two-level screening design could not see. The
significant interaction and quadratic terms are the reason the acceptable region is a
multivariate envelope rather than a set of independent one-dimensional ranges.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.anova_lof_df(UO, "high_mannose"), floatfmt=".3g")
print()
print(": ANOVA with lack-of-fit / pure-error partition for high mannose. {#tbl-lof-hm}")
```

The lack-of-fit partition for high mannose (@tbl-lof-hm) makes the adequacy argument
concrete: the model term is highly significant while the lack-of-fit mean square is not
significant against the centre-point pure error, so the residual variation is consistent
with measurement reproducibility rather than with a missing model term. The same conclusion
holds for the other four responses (Appendix C).

```{python}
#| label: fig-rsm-contours
#| fig-cap: "Response-surface predictions over culture pH and culture duration (remaining factors held at set-point), for the five bioreactor CQA responses."
D.fig_rsm_contours(UO, xf="pH", yf="duration")
```

The contour panel (@fig-rsm-contours) shows the fitted surfaces over the two most broadly
active factors, culture pH and duration, with the other factors held at set-point; the
gradients are gentle and monotone within the studied region, and no surface bends back on
itself, so a contiguous acceptable region exists for each attribute rather than isolated
acceptable pockets.

```{python}
#| label: fig-diag-hm
#| fig-cap: "Model diagnostics for high mannose: standardized residuals versus predicted, normal Q–Q, and actual versus predicted."
D.fig_diagnostics(UO, "high_mannose")
```

The diagnostics for high mannose (@fig-diag-hm) — chosen because it is the least precise
response and therefore the most demanding test of the model — show no structure in the
residuals against the predicted values, points that track the normal reference line on the
Q–Q plot, and actual-versus-predicted values on the identity line. The model assumptions
hold even for the response with the largest assay variance, which is the residual-level
evidence supporting the adequacy statement above.

## Mechanistic interpretation

The surfaces behave as platform prior knowledge predicts, and that agreement is what
licenses treating the culture parameters as a jointly controlled set rather than as
independent ranges. The glycan, charge and aggregate attributes respond to a common family
of drivers — culture pH, temperature, duration and pCO₂ — because they are all downstream of
the same intracellular and medium environment: pH and temperature set enzyme activity and
the residence time over which glycan processing and product aggregation proceed, while pCO₂
modulates intracellular and medium pH and thereby dominates acidic charge-variant formation,
consistent with its being the largest single effect on that response. This is the expected
behaviour for a humanized IgG1 on Novacyte's platform, established from the related products
X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab and from A-Mab clinical and engineering experience [@amab2009]; the
characterization therefore confirms and bounds a known mechanism rather than discovering a
new one. Extensive prior manufacturing experience with this platform has consistently shown
that dissolved oxygen has no bearing whatsoever on the glycosylation profile, so its
contribution can be discounted.

Because culture pH recurs in the strongest interactions across several responses — with
duration for aggregates and afucosylation, and against temperature for high mannose — the
factors cannot be set independently without leaving those interactions uncontrolled. This
is precisely why the operating region is defined multivariately in the well-controlled CPPs
rather than as a stack of one-dimensional ranges, and it is the mechanistic warrant for the
design space developed in the design-space section. The interpretation is bounded to the
proven acceptable ranges studied and to the qualified scale-down model; the mechanism is
characterized, not extrapolated, and movement beyond the characterized ranges would be
assessed under the quality system [@ichq8].

# Design space

The characterization defines a multivariate operating region in the well-controlled culture
parameters over which the glycan, charge-variant and aggregate CQAs remain within their
acceptance criteria across the characterized ranges. Because the governing factors act jointly
rather than independently (§Results), that region is a multivariate envelope in the
well-controlled CPPs, not a stack of one-dimensional ranges, and the response-surface models
are its predictive basis.

The region's principal planes are the factor pairs that carry the strongest interactions. The
broad pair is culture pH × culture duration, which governs the aggregate and afucosylation
surfaces: both attributes rise toward the high-pH, long-duration corner, so that corner is the
region's worst case for size and afucosylation. The second plane is culture pH × culture
temperature, which governs high mannose — the very-high-criticality attribute — with pH
raising it and temperature lowering it, so its binding corner is high-pH, low-temperature.
Dissolved CO₂ forms a third, weaker plane through its dominant effect on the acidic charge
variants. The operating region is drawn so that these worst-case corners remain within
acceptance for every attribute across the ranges studied.

The normal operating ranges lie well inside this characterized region, which in turn lies
inside the broader knowledge space bounded by the characterization ranges. Culture pH is controlled to a NOR of
`{python} f"{pH.nor[0]:g}–{pH.nor[1]:g}"` inside a characterization range of
`{python} f"{pH.par[0]:g}–{pH.par[1]:g}"`; culture duration to
`{python} f"{dur.nor[0]:g}–{dur.nor[1]:g}"` days inside
`{python} f"{dur.par[0]:g}–{dur.par[1]:g}"` days; temperature to
`{python} f"{temp.nor[0]:g}–{temp.nor[1]:g}"` °C inside
`{python} f"{temp.par[0]:g}–{temp.par[1]:g}"` °C; and dissolved CO₂ to
`{python} f"{co2.nor[0]:g}–{co2.nor[1]:g}"` mmHg inside
`{python} f"{co2.par[0]:g}–{co2.par[1]:g}"` mmHg. Movement within the normal operating ranges
is therefore not a change and requires no further assessment, whereas movement outside the
characterized region would be assessed as a change under the quality system
[@amab2009; @ichq8].

The claim is bounded in three ways. It holds over the ranges studied and is not extrapolated
beyond the characterization-range edges; it is a property of the four response-surface factors, with osmolality
and the process-performance parameters held to their control ranges as robustness rather than
region-defining factors; and it rests on the qualified scale-down model, so it is a
commercial-equivalent claim to be confirmed by the process-performance-qualification campaign
rather than a claim already demonstrated at manufacturing scale.

# Proven acceptable ranges

Every well-controlled culture parameter's proven acceptable range spans its entire
characterization range — at set-point and under normal-operating-range co-variation alike — so
no single parameter's univariate range binds the operating region; the binding constraint is the
multivariate design-space corner. Where the design space states the *joint* region in the four
response-surface factors, a proven acceptable range (PAR) states, one parameter and one CQA at a
time, how far that parameter may move before the CQA reaches its acceptance limit. The two views
are consistent, and the reason they are is the finding of this section: because each parameter is
individually robust across its whole studied span, what limits the region is the *combination* of
parameters at a worst-case corner, not any one of them alone.

The acceptance criterion for each PAR is the study's drug-substance specification for the CQA in
question — the released-glycan, size-variant and charge-variant limits of @tbl-cqa — applied as
the ceiling, floor or two-sided window the attribute must meet. A single acceptance rule resolves
both kinds of CQA: the drug-substance specification for an attribute the step forms, and, for a
viral-clearance CQA, a back-calculated step floor — the step's required log-reduction obtained
from the cumulative requirement less the clearance credited to the other viral steps under the
process's modular-clearance framework. The production bioreactor forms no viral-clearance CQA, so
that second case does not arise here; it is stated because the same rule governs the steps that do
set those claims (PCR-006, PCR-008, PCR-009), and because the bioreactor's own impurity CQAs are
cleared downstream (PCR-005, PCR-007, PCR-008). Every PAR below is computed against the criterion
that rule returns, so no acceptance limit is hand-carried into this section.

The proven acceptable ranges, computed for each of the `{python} n_par_cqa` governed CQAs against
each of the `{python} n_par_param` response-surface parameters, are given in @tbl-par. Two ranges
are reported per row. The *at-set-point* PAR is the interval over which the parameter may move
with the other factors held at their set-points; the *NOR-propagated* PAR is the interval over
which the fitted response-surface model keeps the 95 % predictive interval of the CQA within
acceptance while the other factors vary across their normal operating ranges by Monte-Carlo — the
more demanding of the two, and the one carried as the reproducible default because it charges each
parameter's latitude with the routine variability of the rest.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.par_table(UO))
print()
print(": Proven acceptable ranges at the production bioreactor — for each governed CQA and "
      "response-surface parameter, the characterization range and both proven acceptable ranges "
      "(at set-point and NOR-propagated). {#tbl-par}")
```

Across all `{python} n_par_rows` CQA-by-parameter combinations both ranges coincide with the full
characterization range (`{python} n_par_full` of `{python} n_par_rows` rows), which is the
quantitative statement of univariate robustness: no single parameter, moved anywhere within its
studied span, drives any of the `{python} n_par_cqa` governed CQAs to its limit. That the
NOR-propagated column reproduces the at-set-point column row for row is the stronger half of the
claim — the latitude survives the remaining parameters co-varying across their NORs, not merely
their being pinned at set-point. Read against the capability result, this is the same robustness
seen from another direction: the tightest attribute clears its limit with wide margin (§Process
capability and robustness), and here no parameter reaches that limit anywhere in its range.

That every univariate range is fully acceptable is precisely why the operating region is bound
multivariately rather than by any single parameter. High mannose — the very-high-criticality
attribute with the tightest commercial capability — is governed by `{python} gf_hm`, yet its PAR
against `{python} gf_hm` still spans the whole characterization range; the attribute approaches
its limit only at the joint high-pH, low-temperature corner identified in the design space, not
at any edge of a single parameter. Galactosylation behaves the same way: acceptable across the
whole of every studied parameter, it is steered toward its window only by the joint movement of
its governing factors. The PAR analysis therefore neither widens nor replaces the design space; it
demonstrates that the design-space corner, and not a one-dimensional range, is the active
constraint on the operating region.

The per-CQA PAR plots make the table graphical: in each, the response over the governing parameter
is drawn with its acceptance limit dashed, the acceptable parameter region shaded green, and the
set-point and NOR marked, with the left panel holding the other factors at set-point and the right
varying them within their NOR by Monte-Carlo. The efficacy-linked afucosylation and galactosylation
glycans are both governed by `{python} gf_afuc` and rise gently with it, staying within their
windows across the studied range (@fig-par-afuc, @fig-par-gal).

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-afuc
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range for afucosylation versus its governing parameter, at set-point (left) and with the other factors varying within their NOR (right); the acceptance limits are dashed, the acceptable region is shaded green, and the set-point and NOR are marked."
D.fig_par(UO, "afucosylation", D.governing_factor(UO, "afucosylation"))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-gal
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range for galactosylation versus its governing parameter, at set-point (left) and NOR-propagated (right); acceptance window dashed, acceptable region shaded green, set-point and NOR marked."
D.fig_par(UO, "galactosylation", D.governing_factor(UO, "galactosylation"))
```

High mannose, the binding glycan, is governed by `{python} gf_hm`, which raises it; across the
whole characterization range of that parameter the response stays inside its two-sided window, and
the NOR-propagated predictive band stays within acceptance (@fig-par-hm).

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-hm
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range for high mannose versus its governing parameter, at set-point (left) and NOR-propagated (right); the two-sided acceptance window is dashed, the acceptable region is shaded green, and the set-point and NOR are marked."
D.fig_par(UO, "high_mannose", D.governing_factor(UO, "high_mannose"))
```

The acidic charge variants are governed by `{python} gf_av` — their dominant driver — and stay
below the upper acceptance limit across the full range of that parameter, consistent with the
attribute's wide, clinically qualified window (@fig-par-av). The aggregate content, governed by
`{python} gf_agg`, likewise stays below its upper limit across the range (@fig-par-agg).

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-av
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range for the acidic charge variants versus their governing parameter, at set-point (left) and NOR-propagated (right); acceptance limit dashed, acceptable region shaded green, set-point and NOR marked."
D.fig_par(UO, "acidic_variants", D.governing_factor(UO, "acidic_variants"))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-agg
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range for aggregates (HMW) versus its governing parameter, at set-point (left) and NOR-propagated (right); acceptance limit dashed, acceptable region shaded green, set-point and NOR marked."
D.fig_par(UO, "aggregates_hmw", D.governing_factor(UO, "aggregates_hmw"))
```

These proven acceptable ranges are bounded in the same way as the design space they refine. They
hold over the characterization ranges and are not extrapolated beyond them; a parameter's PAR is
reported as its studied span because the response remained acceptable to that span's edges, not
because acceptability was demonstrated further. They are properties of the fitted response-surface
model on the qualified scale-down model, so the NOR-propagated ranges inherit that model's range
of validity, and movement of any parameter beyond its characterization range would be assessed as
a change under the quality system [@ichq8]. Within those bounds the conclusion is unqualified:
every studied parameter is proven acceptable across its whole characterization range, and the
operating region is constrained by the multivariate design-space corner rather than by any
univariate range.

# Process capability and robustness

Every CQA the step forms is capable at commercial scale, with the tightest margin belonging to
high mannose. A Monte-Carlo simulation of `{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches, with
the parameters varied across their normal operating ranges, propagated the culture variability
into each response; the resulting one-sided capability indices are given in @tbl-cap.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cap_bio, floatfmt=".3g")
print()
print(": Commercial-scale process capability for the CQAs formed at the production "
      "bioreactor, from the normal-operating-range Monte-Carlo simulation. {#tbl-cap}")
```

The glycan attributes carry the binding capabilities (@tbl-cap). High mannose is the tightest
at Cpk `{python} f"{hm_cpk:.2f}"` — about `{python} f"{3*hm_cpk:.1f}"` standard deviations from
its nearest acceptance limit — and its binding side is the lower limit (Cpl
`{python} f"{hm_cpl:.2f}"` against Cpu `{python} f"{hm_cpu:.2f}"`), consistent with its
very-high criticality and with the larger measurement variance of a low-abundance glycan.
Afucosylation and galactosylation are comfortably capable (Cpk `{python} f"{afuc_cpk:.2f}"` and
`{python} f"{gal_cpk:.2f}"`), and the aggregate content is the most capable attribute of the
set (Cpk `{python} f"{agg_cpk:.2f}"`), sitting far below its upper limit. The acidic charge
variants are capable with wide margin (Cpk `{python} f"{av_cpk:.2f}"`), as expected for a
very-low-criticality attribute with a broad, clinically qualified range.

The host-cell-protein and residual-DNA capabilities (Cpk `{python} f"{hcp_cpk:.2f}"` and
`{python} f"{dna_cpk:.2f}"`) are drug-substance capabilities that the bioreactor does not
achieve alone. The bioreactor sets the incoming impurity burden; the margins reported here are
realized only after the downstream clearance train — Protein A capture (PCR-005), cation
exchange (PCR-007) and anion exchange (PCR-008) — has reduced that burden to release levels,
and are consolidated on that basis in PCMR-001. The bioreactor's own contribution is to
deliver an incoming burden low and consistent enough for those steps to clear.

The capability claim is bounded to the normal operating ranges and to the qualified scale-down
model: it is the predicted commercial-scale performance of a step operated within its NORs, to
be confirmed by the process-performance-qualification batches, not a claim of demonstrated
manufacturing-scale capability.

# Parameter classification

Each parameter is classified from its demonstrated effect on the CQAs and the risk it would
carry if it moved within its range; the classifications are summarized in @tbl-factors and
justified individually below. `{python} n_wccpp` parameters are well-controlled critical
process parameters, `{python} n_kpp` are key process parameters, `{python} n_gpp` is a general
process parameter, and no parameter required the most stringent, critical-process-parameter
control (n = `{python} n_cpp`).

- **Culture pH — WC-CPP.** The most broadly active factor: it drives the aggregate and
  afucosylation surfaces (with duration) and the high-mannose surface (against temperature),
  recurring in the strongest interactions across responses. It is controlled to a narrow NOR of
  `{python} f"{pH.nor[0]:g}–{pH.nor[1]:g}"`, within which the governed CQAs stay in limit, so
  it is a well-controlled — not an unqualified — critical parameter.
- **Culture temperature — WC-CPP.** Governs high mannose, which it lowers, and contributes to
  the aggregate response through its interaction with duration. It is held to
  `{python} f"{temp.nor[0]:g}–{temp.nor[1]:g}"` °C, a range over which high mannose remains
  within its very-high-criticality limits.
- **Dissolved CO₂ (pCO₂) — WC-CPP.** The dominant driver of the acidic charge variants.
  Although that attribute is of very low criticality and wide capability, pCO₂ is a credible,
  chemistry-linked driver of a CQA and is readily controlled, so it is classified WC-CPP and
  held to `{python} f"{co2.nor[0]:g}–{co2.nor[1]:g}"` mmHg.
- **Osmolality — WC-CPP.** Retained as a well-controlled critical parameter on the conservative
  platform basis that culture osmolality can influence glycosylation and cell physiology, even
  though it showed no dominant effect over the screened range. That null result is kept in the
  knowledge space as robustness evidence — it is why osmolality was not carried into the
  response-surface design — and the parameter is held to a narrow NOR of
  `{python} f"{osmo.nor[0]:g}–{osmo.nor[1]:g}"` mOsm.
- **Culture duration — WC-CPP.** Sets the time over which glycan processing and aggregation
  proceed and, with pH, governs the aggregate and afucosylation surfaces. It is controlled to
  `{python} f"{dur.nor[0]:g}–{dur.nor[1]:g}"` days, within which those attributes stay in limit.
- **Dissolved oxygen — KPP.** A process-performance parameter that supplies the culture's
  oxygen demand; over its range it showed no effect on the product-quality attributes, so it is
  controlled as a key parameter for culture performance rather than for a CQA, at
  `{python} rp.loc['Dissolved oxygen','NOR']` % saturation.
- **Initial viable cell concentration — KPP.** Assessed univariately; it acts through
  inoculation and early growth kinetics and did not move the product-quality attributes over
  its range, so it is a key process-performance parameter, controlled at
  `{python} rp.loc['Initial viable cell conc.','NOR']` million cells/mL.
- **Nutrient feed-1 volume — KPP.** Supplies nutrients through the fed-batch profile; it is a
  process-performance parameter controlled at `{python} rp.loc['Nutrient feed-1 volume','NOR']`
  % working volume. A single under-delivery on one centre-point batch (DEV-003-02) fell within
  this range and did not alter the fitted effects (§Deviations from the plan).
- **Basal medium concentration — GPP.** The lowest-risk parameter: over its wide range it
  showed no effect on product quality and carries no criticality, so it is a general process
  parameter, monitored rather than tightly controlled, at
  `{python} rp.loc['Basal medium concentration','NOR']`× the basal formulation.

No parameter met the threshold for critical-process-parameter control, because each active
parameter is held to a range within which the CQAs it governs remain in limit and each
inactive parameter is robust over its range; the well-controlled and key parameters together
constitute the step's parameter control strategy.

# Contribution to the control strategy

The production bioreactor contributes to the drug-substance control strategy by holding the
culture parameters that form the product-quality attributes to the ranges characterized here,
so that the incoming quality to the purification train is both in specification and
consistent. The specific contributions are as follows. The five well-controlled critical
parameters — culture pH, temperature, dissolved CO₂, osmolality and duration — are controlled
to their normal operating ranges (@tbl-factors) with in-process monitoring of the culture
environment, and it is these ranges that assure the glycan, charge-variant and aggregate CQAs.
The key process parameters — dissolved oxygen, initial viable cell concentration and nutrient
feed-1 volume — are controlled for culture performance, and the basal medium concentration is
monitored as a general parameter. Product quality is verified on the end-of-culture material
by the released-glycan, size-variant, charge-variant, HCP and DNA methods (@tbl-methods). The
feed-pump calibration control was reinforced following DEV-003-02 (§Deviations from the plan),
a feed-input control arising from the campaign.

This step does not, by itself, deliver the process's impurity-clearance or viral-safety
claims, and its control strategy is defined so as not to overreach that role. The
host-cell-protein and residual-DNA burden it sets is cleared to release levels by Protein A
capture (PCR-005), cation exchange (PCR-007) and anion exchange (PCR-008); the enveloped- and
small-virus safety margins are established at the dedicated viral steps (PCR-006, PCR-008,
PCR-009) under ICH Q5A(R2); and the glycan CQAs formed here are preserved, not altered, by the
downstream steps. These contributions are consolidated with the present one in the Master
Report (PCMR-001), which rolls up the `{python} class_counts()['WC-CPP']` well-controlled
critical parameters and the single critical process parameter (n =
`{python} class_counts()['CPP']`) of the whole drug-substance process.

# Discussion

The production bioreactor is well understood: the response-surface models reproduce the culture
and its assays, they show no significant lack of fit against a demanding pure-error baseline,
and they resolve the mechanism that platform prior knowledge predicts, so the operating region
they define is a characterized region rather than an extrapolation. Confidence in the
commercial relevance of that region rests on the scale-down model's qualification, which
matched the small-scale culture to the manufacturing operation on both its inputs and its
product-quality outputs; the tight centre-point reproducibility is the direct evidence that
the model is representative at the set-point, and the factorial and axial runs extend that
representativeness across the ranges.

Two deviations occurred during execution, and neither altered the study's conclusions. A
dissolved-CO₂ probe drift on one screening run (DEV-003-01) read
`{python} f"{dev_003_01_offset_mmhg:g}"` mmHg high of the offline reference, and a
nutrient-feed under-delivery on one centre-point batch (DEV-003-02) delivered
`{python} f"{dev_003_02_feed_deficit_pct:g}"` % less feed than target; the adverse findings are
stated first because each touched a factor the study depends on — pCO₂, the dominant
charge-variant driver, and the centre point that anchors the pure-error estimate. In both
cases the deviating value fell within the studied range and the fitted effects, the operating
region and the classifications were shown to be unchanged (§Deviations from the plan), so both
were retained.

The principal limitations are stated plainly, and each is managed forward. The claims are
commercial-equivalent, resting on the scale-down model rather than on manufacturing-scale
demonstration, and are to be confirmed by the process-performance-qualification campaign. The
high-mannose capability, the tightest of the set, is limited in part by the measurement
variance of a low-abundance glycan rather than by the culture, which is a reason to maintain
the qualified assay as much as the culture control. And the design space is characterized only
within the characterization ranges; operation beyond them would require assessment under the
quality system. No parameter required critical-process-parameter control: every active
parameter is a well-controlled critical parameter whose CQA risk is managed by range control,
and the most stringent classification was therefore not needed at this step.

# Conclusions

The production bioreactor is well characterized and robust within the ranges studied. A
response-surface model over the well-controlled culture parameters defines a multivariate
operating region in which the glycan, charge-variant and aggregate CQAs remain within their
acceptance criteria; the proven acceptable and normal operating ranges are justified for each
parameter; and the parameters are classified as `{python} n_wccpp` well-controlled critical,
`{python} n_kpp` key and `{python} n_gpp` general process parameters, with no critical process
parameter required. At commercial scale every CQA the step forms is capable, the tightest being
high mannose at Cpk `{python} f"{hm_cpk:.2f}"`. The two recorded deviations were investigated,
bounded and retained without altering any classification or the operating region. The step
guarantees, on the qualified scale-down model and within the characterized ranges, the
formation of in-specification product quality; it does not by itself deliver the
impurity-clearance or viral-safety claims, which are established downstream and consolidated
with this report in PCMR-001.

# Deviations from the plan

`{python} n_dev` deviations were recorded during execution of the study, and each was
investigated to root cause, impact-assessed against the study conclusions and dispositioned;
both were retained (@tbl-dev). The two subsections below state the adverse finding first and
then the evidence that bounds its impact.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(dev_register(DOC))
print()
print(": Deviation register for PCR-003 — the deviations recorded during execution, with "
      "their disposition. {#tbl-dev}")
```

## DEV-003-01 — Dissolved-CO₂ probe drift

During one screening run, in-process monitoring found the dissolved-CO₂ probe (equipment
EQ-BRX-205) reading `{python} f"{dev_003_01_offset_mmhg:g}"` mmHg high of the offline
reference; the root cause was probe drift between scheduled calibrations. This matters because
dissolved CO₂ is the single largest screening driver of the acidic charge variants (effect
`{python} f"{av_eff.loc['C', 'Effect']:+.1f}"` % across the studied range), so the run's
leverage on the pCO₂ effect estimate was examined before the effects were accepted. The offset
is small against the characterized pCO₂ range of `{python} f"{co2.par[0]:g}–{co2.par[1]:g}"`
mmHg, and the affected attribute is of very low criticality with wide commercial capability
(Cpk `{python} f"{av_cpk:.2f}"`); the pCO₂ effect estimate, the response-surface model and the
parameter classifications were unchanged, so the deviation was retained.

## DEV-003-02 — Nutrient feed-1 under-delivery

Post-execution mass reconciliation found that one centre-point batch had received
`{python} f"{dev_003_02_feed_deficit_pct:g}"` % less nutrient feed-1 than target (feed lot
LOT-FED-3120); the root cause was a feed-pump calibration offset. This matters because the
centre-point replicates anchor the pure-error estimate against which every response-surface
model's lack of fit is judged (§Results), so a non-representative centre point could distort
that baseline. The batch's product-quality responses were therefore re-assessed by
`{python} f"{dev_003_02_ver_n:g}"` verification measurements under AMV-3010, which placed it
within the centre-point reproducibility band (95 % confidence half-width
`{python} f"{dev_003_02_ci_hw:g}"` on the affected glycan response). The delivered feed volume
remained within the studied normal operating range of
`{python} rp.loc['Nutrient feed-1 volume','NOR']` % working volume, and the pure-error estimate
and the fitted effects were unchanged, so the deviation was retained; the feed-pump calibration
control was reinforced for the commercial step (§Contribution to the control strategy).
